newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on late cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on late cover.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates reversed earlier increases to close down 55 basis points at 22.85 percent on Thursday on a late scrable to cover positions after a volatile session, traders said.
"The market is awash with liquidity, but a weakening peso triggered speculation and some had to buy at low rates to cover positions at the close," a trader said.
Overnight Cetes rates reached a high of 24.10 percent during the session.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 2.8 centavos weaker at 7.8310/7.8360 per dollar.

Other traders said pressure on rates was due to the central bank draining liquidity from the system by holding six auctions to purchase 5.409 billion pesos of paper, which it assigned at between 24.76 and 25.92 percent.
"Banco de Mexico is still draining plenty of liquidity, and assigned auctions at much higher rates than in recent sessions," another trader said.
Traders said Banco drained surplus liquidity arising from government spending of some four billion pesos during the session.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 20 basis points at 24.50 percent, but off a session high of 25.00 percent.

Traders said they expected secondary interest rates to remain stable in the coming sessions. Nonetheless, they saw liquidity pressures arising ahead of the cutoff date for banks to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank on Jan 22.
Liquidity of 755 million pesos was expected to return to the system on Friday.
